title: Data Scientist
summary: Senior Data Scientist with 8+ years turning large datasets into actionable insight across Healthcare, Telecom and AIOps, with an MSc in Machine Learning and AI. Writes production SQL and PySpark pipelines, builds statistical and machine learning models for prediction, anomaly detection and forecasting, and defines evaluation metrics for ML and LLM systems. Summarises and communicates findings to stakeholders in a way that shapes priorities. Alongside this, I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD.

project.name: Model Release Experiment Analysis
bullets: Built an experiment analysis toolkit for comparing ML model versions across real and simulated test scenarios, using SQL and PySpark to assemble datasets and statsmodels for hypothesis testing.

Checked distribution and test assumptions, reported effect sizes with bootstrap confidence intervals, and shared findings through Power BI dashboards that guided which model issues engineers fixed first.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Data Scientist role in Data Quality and Provenance. My data science work has always ended in a decision: which system to fix, which alarm to trust, which model is good enough to ship. Turning large, messy datasets into findings that engineering teams act on is the thread through my career.

Wayve is teaching vehicles to drive through learned models rather than maps, and in that world the quality of the data and the metrics decides what gets better. That is work I care about. My fiancée lives in Berlin, and we plan to move to Stuttgart, Germany together and settle there long term.

I would bring strong SQL and a habit of turning analysis into priorities. At Nippon Data Systems I built SQL and PySpark pipelines on large healthcare datasets that cut manual reporting effort by 95%. At United Health Group I defined evaluation metrics for question answering and summary agents that reduced human review by 43%.

Outside work I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD. It reminds me to measure whether something truly helps before trusting it. I would be glad to talk about how I could support your engineering teams.
